media_strategy.selection_principle: default to all five channels (chart, image, video, audio, interactive); each chosen because the dataset's properties (digit ranks, transition matrix, run lengths, substring search) reward those forms; no quota-driven additions

chart.reason: Pi's digits are intrinsically quantitative — a 10x10 transition heatmap, per-digit bar/error chart, and a log-x convergence plot are the natural primitives.

image.reason: Three atmospheric stills (hero digit-cluster, Feynman-point row, mainframe printout) provide editorial breaks between dense statistical sections.

video.reason: image2video animates the hero still so the page feels alive at the top without a separate narrative video.

audio.reason: A short ambient marimba bed evokes 'random but musical' — paired with a play button and a clear visual fallback.

interactive_or_map.reason: A 'where in pi?' substring search lookup lets the reader feel the surprise of '0123456789' being absent and '999999' arriving at decimal 762.

des_01.label: Teaser hero still — golden cluster of digits

content.prompt: Macro overhead shot of a sea of glowing decimal digits 0 through 9, rendered as light-trails flowing across a deep midnight blue void, with one bright golden cluster of six 9s catching the light at the center; cinematic editorial photograph, sharp depth of field, no text labels visible, 16:9 aspect ratio, hero image for a mathematics blog about pi

des_01.brief: Full-bleed cinematic hero showing pi's million digits as light-trails on a midnight field, with the Feynman-point cluster glowing gold in the middle. Sets up the entire piece visually before any prose.
des_01.rationale: A still image generates atmosphere and curiosity; the gold cluster is a visual breadcrumb to the Feynman-point reveal in edt_04.

des_02.label: Teaser motion — animated push-in

content.prompt: Slow parallax push-in toward the central golden cluster of six 9s; ambient particles drift gently across the frame; subtle warm flicker on the lit cluster; no camera shake

des_02.brief: 6-second autoplaying-muted-loop animation of the teaser. Adds kinetic energy without losing the still composition. Plays once when scrolled into view; reader sees the gold cluster slowly approach.
des_02.rationale: We already invested in the hero still; image2video is the highest leverage way to animate it. Using muted autoplay keeps the page accessible.

des_03.label: Hero stat strip — chi-squared p-value

content.label: Chi-squared test against uniform digits — a fair die would do worse 79% of the time.

des_03.brief: Three stacked stat callouts at the top of edt_01: '1,000,001 digits', 'p = 0.7874 (uniform)', 'p = 0.6172 (pairwise)'. Large 64-72px display numbers, small descriptive labels.
des_03.rationale: The two p-values are the spine of the whole argument; presenting them as a hero stat strip lets the rest of the post be the explanation.

des_04.label: Per-digit count chart with error bars

content.interaction: hover tooltip with exact count and deviation

style.palette: warm-gray with one accent gold for digit 9

des_04.brief: Lollipop chart: x = digit 0..9, y = observed percentage with 95% binomial CI bars. Horizontal dashed line at 10%. y-axis zoomed to [9.85%, 10.15%] so the 0.05pp deviations are visible. Digit 6 (lowest) and digit 5 (highest) get small annotations.
des_04.rationale: Bars without error bars would imply spurious differences; the CIs make visible that every digit is statistically indistinguishable from 10%.

des_05.label: 10x10 transition matrix heatmap

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing P(j|i)% and absolute count

des_05.brief: 10x10 cell heatmap. Diverging color centered at exactly 10.00%; deviations of 0.25pp barely shift the hue, which is the whole point. Diagonal cells get a thin outline. Below the chart: small caption noting the chi-squared statistic.
des_05.rationale: This is the visual centerpiece of the post — a deliberately featureless heatmap that proves featureless-ness statistically.

des_06.label: Self-transition gauge strip

content.what_each_panel_shows: One arc per digit: arc length proportional to self_pct, scale [9.7%, 10.3%]; reference tick at 10%; numerical pct shown beneath
content.color: single accent (deep teal); reference line in light gray

des_06.brief: Ten compact arc gauges in a 2x5 grid. Each shows P(i->i) as an arc against a 10% baseline. Inspired by the original TidyTuesday hero figure but reproduced in our color palette.
des_06.rationale: Honors the dataset submitter's hero figure while integrating it into the blog's visual language. Compact enough to live mid-article without dominating.

des_07.label: Atmospheric still — Feynman-point row

content.prompt: Cinematic close-up photograph of a single old library page with one row of decimal digits zoomed in; the row contains the sequence 999999 highlighted by a faint warm glow; surrounding rows are blurred bokeh of small printed numbers; matte ink-on-paper texture, soft warm desk lamp; serene, contemplative

des_07.brief: Print-on-paper-style still that visually anchors the Feynman-point story. Provides a moment of breathing room before the bar chart of longest runs.
des_07.rationale: A photograph of digits-on-paper turns an abstract finding into a tangible artifact. Stronger than a generic 'six 9s' graphic.

des_08.label: Longest-run bar chart with starting positions

highlight.digit_9: row highlighted in gold; subtitle: 'Feynman point (decimal 762)'
highlight.digit_3: row highlighted in teal; subtitle: 'longest overall: 7 in a row'

des_08.brief: Horizontal bar chart with one bar per digit. Bar length = longest streak (5..7). Each bar labeled with its starting decimal position. Digits 9 (Feynman point) and 3 (the lone 7-run) are visually highlighted.
des_08.rationale: Two facts in one chart — how long each digit's longest run is, and where it lands in the million decimals.

des_09.label: Substring lookup interactive

content.initial_state: A table of famous strings ('42', '666', '999999', '0123456789', '123456789', etc.) showing 'first decimal place' or 'NOT in first 1M (textbook position: 17,387,594,880)'
content.trigger: Reader can also type a 1- to 6-digit string into a text box; backend is a precomputed lookup of all length<=6 first-occurrence positions inlined as JSON
content.transition: Result row appears below the input: 'Found at decimal place X' or 'Not found in first 1,000,000 decimals'
content.payoff: Reader feels the boundary at length 6 directly — most short strings are present; many 6-digit dates aren't.

des_09.brief: Interactive featuring (a) a static table of headline substrings with their first-occurrence positions, (b) a small input box where the reader can type a 1-to-6-digit string and see whether it appears, and where. Implementation note: the Programmer should ship a precomputed lookup of first-occurrences for all length-<=6 strings, but only inline a curated demo set (the famous strings + a small random sample) to keep the page lightweight. For arbitrary inputs, the JS computes position by linear scan of a string of pi's first 100k decimals (small enough to inline as a 100KB string).
des_09.rationale: The 'birthday in pi' parlor trick is exactly the interaction this dataset was made for. Even a tiny inline pi string makes the experience real.

des_10.label: Coverage by length stat strip

style.title: Fraction of length-k strings present in 1M decimals

des_10.brief: Compact dot plot: four points (k=4..7), each showing observed coverage with a tiny ghost marker for theoretical expected coverage. Highlights how 'birthday in pi' breaks at k=6.
des_10.rationale: Pairs the substring lookup with the underlying probability so the reader understands why some 6-digit strings are missing.

des_11.label: Convergence to 10% — log-x ten-line chart

content.highlight: annotate digit 7 (slowest to settle, n=368,515) at end of its line
content.interaction: hover shows running pct at that n; legend toggles individual digits

des_11.brief: Ten lines, one per digit. X-axis log-scaled n. Y-axis zoomed to highlight late-stage convergence. Reference line at 10%. Digit 7 is the visible 'slowpoke' that takes longest to settle.
des_11.rationale: Log-x is the only honest x-axis for this story; with linear x we'd see ten flat lines and no convergence drama.

des_12.label: Atmospheric still — mainframe printout of digits

content.prompt: Editorial close-up photograph of a 1970s mainframe printer slowly extruding a long tractor-feed paper strip filled with computed decimal digits, paper cascading onto the floor; warm desk lamp light; analog scientific atmosphere; no readable specific numbers, just the texture of densely printed digits

des_12.brief: Closing atmospheric still. Lets the closing prose breathe; provides a counterpoint to NASA-only-needs-15-digits.
des_12.rationale: Edt_07 is reflective; a photograph of a printout grounds the philosophical close in the physical history of computing pi.

des_13.label: Ambient marimba bed

content.why_audio: Pi's digits are 'random but musical'; a short ambient marimba bed reinforces the emotional point that the convergence chart makes visually.
content.trigger: Click 'Listen' button beneath the convergence chart
content.ui_form: compact play/pause button inline with the chart; never autoplays

content.prompt: Ten short marimba notes, one per digit 0-9, very gentle and contemplative; no bass, no drums, soft ambient pad underneath; calm minimalist mathematics-museum atmosphere; 10 seconds, no vocals

content.fallback: If audio is muted or unsupported, the convergence chart alone tells the story; the play button is purely optional.
content.novelty_note: This is a discreet ambient bed, not a click-to-play tone card or a sonification UI.

des_13.brief: A 10-second ambient marimba clip available behind a small play button under the convergence chart. Optional, never autoplay, paired with a visual fallback (the chart itself).
des_13.rationale: Audio is included by default; this is the most restrained form that doesn't distract from the analytical sections.

des_14.label: Reference image (TidyTuesday original)

content.prompt: (reference image — included with attribution to Manasseh Oduor, TidyTuesday community)

des_14.brief: Honor the original TidyTuesday hero figure by including it as a small reference panel alongside our re-implementation, with attribution.
des_14.rationale: Crediting the dataset submitter while showing how our visual language reinterprets the same data is good editorial practice.

page_rhythm.tone: deep editorial — midnight blue + ivory + restrained gold accent for highlights (Feynman point, digit 5, digit 9). Type set in a serif body with a sans display.
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first at edt_01 (teaser + stat strip), then alternating: chart, prose, chart, prose; image atmospheric breaks before edt_04 and edt_07; the heatmap (des_05) at edt_03 is the centerpiece.
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: No card-deck pattern, no map (none would make sense), no quiz interaction (the reveal is statistical, not surprising-fact); the substring lookup is a typing-driven experience rather than a guess-button. Audio is a discreet ambient bed, not a click-to-play tone or chart sonification card.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: 64-72px stat numbers; serif italic for pull quotes; one orange-gold accent reserved for Feynman-point references; chart x/y labels are small caps; full-width hero teaser, but body charts are constrained to a 720px reading column.
